correctness.rationale: For A=I₂ the corrected residual is (I−zzᵀ)E_D. Maximizing zᵀE_DE_Dᵀz leaves the smaller squared diagonal defect, α² min(S₁²,S₂²)/D². Centered programming maps one step to the full Cartesian product of two fair signs under (S₁+S₂,S₁−S₂), so the two D-step walks are independent and the minimum is one fourth of the squared difference of their absolute values. This gives (D−m_D²)/2 before rescaling. In the one-sided model S₁+S₂=D and the minimum is (D−|U_D|)²/4. Conditioning on the walk location gives m_{n+1}−m_n=Pr(U_n=0); the two stated binomial formulas satisfy this recursion at each parity and m₀=0. Stirling gives m_D=√(2D/π)(1+O(1/D)), yielding both limits and the stated remainder. D=1 gives zero; at D=2 distinct directions occur with probability 1/2 and give loss α²/4. At every D≥2 the event of all positive signs and both coordinates selected has positive probability, establishing strict expected loss, not almost-sure rank two. Directly summing the diagonal second moments gives the two decreasing uncorrected risks.

value.rationale: The exact risk distinguishes a centered defect that decays at a known 1/D constant from a biased defect with a positive floor, even though the uncorrected risk decreases in both. The single-to-double-copy comparison demonstrates the failure of exact correction even with perfect information and no read noise. Together these are a quantitative benchmark for deciding what copy averaging and a fixed correction rank can accomplish, not simply the previously known nonmonotonicity caveat.
residual_risks: This is a two-mode operator-loss benchmark, not a hardware performance, solver convergence, or finite-probe result.
